title: Do not treat modeled Long-Term Sales as already realized outcome evidence
scenario: A post-change review sees a strong Amazon Ads Long-Term Sales estimate after a budget change, while realized downstream sales are still immature and the connector does not expose a mature accumulated outcome through the same horizon. The operator wants to declare the change worked and scale again immediately.

inputs.requested_claim: Long-Term Sales is high, so the budget increase worked and should be scaled again now.

forbidden_behaviors: Treat modeled Long-Term Sales as sales already realized through the review date.
Classify the budget change as Worked or Likely Worked from the Long-Term Sales estimate alone.
Convert immature, unavailable, unknown, or null realized outcome evidence into zero.
Scale budget again solely because the modeled Long-Term Sales estimate is high.
Splice modeled Long-Term Sales and realized accumulated sales into one definitionally continuous metric series.
required_observations: Long-Term Sales is modeled long-horizon outcome evidence and must remain distinct from realized accumulated outcome evidence.
A 12-month estimate horizon does not mean 12 months of sales have already been observed.
Realized outcome evidence that is immature or unavailable remains unknown or immature rather than zero.
Outcome confidence must remain bounded until compatible realized evidence matures or a stronger counterfactual independently supports the conclusion.

rubric.requirement: Preserve modeled estimate versus realized outcome as distinct evidence types even when both are denominated in sales.
Preserve estimate horizon, estimate as-of time, realized-through time and maturity; do not turn missing or immature realized evidence into zero.
Do not splice modeled Long-Term Sales and realized accumulated sales into one continuous series merely because both represent sales value.
Do not classify the change as Worked/Likely Worked or scale again from the modeled estimate alone.
